59: ## Setup
60: ​
61: We use npm+brew+stacks to setup and run the project.
62: Node is required preinstalled. [Check Why Node?](./doc/TechDecisions.md#why-node?)
63: ​
64: As part of `npm install` we trigger the shell scripts to setup the project dependencies automatically.
65: ​
66: > For M1 macs please complete Steps 1-4 from Manual Steps section before running, `npm install`.
67: ​
68: ### Auto-Setup
69: ​
70: Auto setup scripts will try to complete all setup steps to get a local version of app running.
71: ​
72: Installing node modules will run other setup scripts on postinstall step:
73: ```
74: npm i
75: ```
76: or 
77: ```
78: npm install
79: ```
80: ​
81: Wait for node packages to install and auto setup script to run.
82: ​
83: If auto-setup script fails try manual steps listed below.
84: ​
85: ### Manual Steps
86: ​
87: Manual steps are a documented version of our auto-setup script.
88: Each step needs to be successful for app to run.
89: ​
90: #### Installation
91: Installation and setup may vary based on OS/Platform being used.
92: You can refer below guide to setup based manually.
93: Before continuing with the installation it is assumed that you have completed [mac basics](https://www.apple.com/voiceover/info/guide/_1122.html) .
94: 
95: #### For M1/M2/M2 PRO Macs
96: Things become complicated for M1 mac systems since not all libs have arm architecture support.
97: Rosetta is used to setup on M1.
98: ​
99:  1. Open LaunchPad
100:  2. Search for Terminal
101:  3. Right click on Terminal application and click on GetInfo, enable open using Rosetta
102:  4. open terminal
103:  5. run `softwareupdate --install-rosetta` in terminal (in case of M2 PRO its already up-to-date)
104:  6. run `arch -x86_64 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/master/install.sh)"` in terminal
105:  7. run `arch -x86_64 /usr/local/bin/brew install haskell-stack postgresql@12 openssl pkg-config redis` in terminal
106:  8. run `echo $0` in terminal
107:     If it returns `zsh`, then run  `echo 'export PATH="/usr/local/opt/postgresql@12/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc`
108:  9. run `source ~/.zshrc` in terminal
109:  10. run `pg_config` if nothing shows up, relaunch terminal.
110: ​
111: #### Other systems
112: 
113: Follow these steps to set up the required dependencies on Linux and other non-Mac systems:
114: 
115: 1. Install stack - Visit [Haskell Stack documentation](https://docs.haskellstack.org/en/stable/README/) for your platform-specific installation instructions.
116: 2. Install postgresql@12 - Use your system's package manager (apt, yum, dnf, pacman, etc.) to install PostgreSQL version 12.
117: 3. Install openssl - Install the OpenSSL development libraries using your system's package manager.
118: 4. Install pkg-config - This utility is needed to help find and compile packages. Install via your package manager.
119: 5. Install redis - Install Redis server using your system's package manager for caching and session storage.
120: #### Setup
121: Few libs will required to be setup and made active for app to run.
122: ##### Postgres database with heartbeat table
123: ​
124: Vayu checks for heartbeat table as a basic requirement to verify db connectivity.
125: It also needs a running redis server locally for temp storage.
126: ##### Adding database
127: ​
128: 1. run `psql postgres` in terminal
129: 2. run `CREATE DATABASE zeyphr;`
130: 3. run `\q` 
131: 4. run `psql zeyphr` to confirm database creation
132: 5. now you can create tables in the said database
133: ​

375: # API Testing with CATS
376: 
377: This project uses the Contract Automated Testing Suite (CATS) for automated testing of the API against the OpenAPI 3.0 specification.
378: 
379: CATS executes during continuous integration to validate that the API's responses adhere to the contract defined in the OpenAPI definition (merged.yaml).
380: 
381: ## CATS Testing
382: 
383: To execute the CATS test cases locally:
384: 
385: ```bash
386: npm run test:cats:commit
387: ```
388: This will invoke the CATS test script defined in package.json as follows:
389: 
390: ` "test:cats:commit": "./scripts/cats/helper/init-test.sh"`
391: 
392: ## CATS Configuration
393: 
394: The key configuration options for CATS are:
395: 
396: `--contract` - The path to the OpenAPI 3.0 spec file to test against.
397: 
398: `--server` - The base URL of the API server to send requests to during testing.
399: 
400: `--headers` - Path to file containing any required headers like authentication.
401: 
402: `--refData` - Path to mock data to use in tests.
403: 
404: **Note:** 
405: Whoever adding new end points in `api.yaml` should also add `x-test : false` in the end point definition for now. This will be removed once the CATS test cases are fixed.
406: 
407: ## CATS Local Setup
408: 
409: Current CATS setup to run tests locally includes only 2 dependencies: `brew` and `docker`
410: With the 2 setup on your machine, you should be able to run CATS relatively easily.
411: 
412: CATS setup architecture currently includes a docker compose file which runs 3 containers:
413: 1. postgres with a db dump supporting currently enabled test cases
414: 2. redis
415: 3. cats-server which runs both the CATS jar and the mock cats server
416: 
417: _Note_: Since postgres and redis are run on their default ports in docker, we shut down running postgres and redis service on local machine during cats execution. If for any reason cats execution is interrupted, the services are not resurrected. Using `brew services run <service_name>` they can be resumed.
418: 
419: ### Execution Flow
420: 1. Check for brew and docker to be present. If brew is not setup or docker is not installed, setup exits
421: 2. Start Docker Desktop
422: 3. Kill running vayu server 
423: 4. Launch terminal window running docker compose
424: 5. Launch terminal window running vayu
425: 6. Wait for CATS execution to complete
426: 7. Exit if errors found otherwise continue to next script
427: 
428: ### Common Pitfalls
429: The cats run script tries to account for many possible local setup cases but sometimes errors can still occur. Following are steps to follow to restore to defaults (follow in order iteratively checking if cats is fixed)
430: 1. Delete cats docker containers
431: 2. Delete cats docker images
432: 3. Stop postgres service
433: 4. Check that docker is exported correctly in .zshrc (or .bashrc or whatever)
434: 5. VPN cannot be used while running cats test cases since shopify calls will fail

1: # Vayu — Claude Code Instructions
2: 
3: Full documentation lives in `plan/` (15 files, 00-14). Read those before any non-trivial work. This file distills the critical rules that prevent the most common mistakes.
4: 
5: ## Golden Rules
6: 
7: 1. **NEVER edit files under `src/Vayu/Generated/`.** All changes go through YAML specs (`doc/schemas/`, `doc/paths/`) + regeneration (`pnpm run generate:api:backend`).
8: 
9: 2. **NEVER write code that can crash at runtime.** No function should produce a possible runtime error. Specifically:
10:    - **NEVER use `fromJust`** — use pattern matching, `fromMaybe`, or `maybe` instead
11:    - **NEVER use `head`/`tail` on potentially empty lists** — use pattern matching or `listToMaybe`
12:    - **NEVER use `undefined` or `error`** — use `Either`/`Maybe` for error handling
13:    - **NEVER use `read`** for parsing — use `readMaybe` or proper parsers
14:    - **NEVER use `!!` for list indexing** — use `listToMaybe`, `take`/`drop`, or `Data.Map`
15:    - **NEVER suppress pattern warnings** with `{-# OPTIONS -fno-warn-incomplete-patterns #-}` or `{-# OPTIONS -fno-warn-incomplete-uni-patterns #-}`
16:    - **ALL case matches on enums MUST be exhaustive** — either handle every constructor or include a wildcard default that returns a safe value (e.g., `_ -> return Nothing`). Missing cases crash the pod when new enum values are added to YAML.
17: 
18: 3. **Prefer operator-style monadic composition over `do` blocks.** Use `>>=`, `>>`, `<&>`, `>.`, `>$`, `>>=?` from `Vayu.Utils.Maybe`. Reserve `do` for complex flows with 3+ reused intermediate bindings or nested case analysis. Short chains (1-2 steps) should always use operators.
19: 
20: ## Code Generation Pipeline
21: 
22: Three separate pipelines, each with their own input spec:
23: 
24: | Pipeline | Input | Command | Output |
25: |----------|-------|---------|--------|
26: | Types + API | `doc/Api.yaml` | `pnpm run generate:api:backend` | `Types/Common/*`, `Types/Storage/*`, `API.hs`, `Accessor.hs` |
27: | DB Queries | `doc/DBQueries.yaml` | `pnpm run generate:db:backend` | `Queries/*.hs` |
28: | Network Calls | `doc/NetworkCalls.yaml` | `pnpm run generate:network:backend` | `NetworkCalls/*.hs` |
29: 
30: The main command (`generate:api:backend`) runs all three.
31: 
32: ## Layered Architecture
33: 
34: ```
35: Generated/API.hs → Core.hs → Product/*.Main → Services/Internal (domain logic + queries)
36:                                              → Services/External (external API calls)
37: ```
38: 
39: - `src/Vayu/Generated/API.hs` maps each `operationId` to `CoreRoutes.<fn>`
40: - `src/Vayu/Routes/Core.hs` — route handlers, auth middleware, context setup (no logging)
41: - `src/Vayu/Product/` — **orchestration layer**: links multiple services, handles logging
42: - `src/Vayu/Services/Internal/` — single-domain business logic, exports Generated queries
43: - `src/Vayu/Services/External/` — external API integrations
44: - `src/Vayu/Utils/` — utilities
45: - `src/Vayu/Types/` — hand-written types (not for API/DB)
46: 
47: ### Product layer rules
48: - Product links domains together (Cart + Customer + Shipping). Single-domain logic belongs in Services/Internal.
49: - Product MUST use `withProductAPILogging` / `withFunctionLogging` from `Vayu.Product.Logger` (one-line wrappers)
50: - Product MUST NOT import from `Generated/Queries`, `Generated/Types/Storage`, or `Storage/Queries` directly — go through Services/Internal
51: - Product CAN import `Storage/Redis` directly — Redis is generic cache ops, wrapping in a service layer would be overkill
52: - Product CAN import other Product modules for cross-domain orchestration
53: 
54: ## Type Mapping (YAML → Haskell)
55: 
56: | OpenAPI | Haskell |
57: |---------|---------|
58: | `type: string` | `Text` |
59: | `type: integer` | `Int` |
60: | `type: number` / `format: double` | `Scientific` |
61: | `type: boolean` | `Bool` |
62: | `type: string, format: date-time` | `LocalTime` |
63: | `type: string, format: date` | `UTCTime` |
64: | `type: object` (freeform) | `Value` (Aeson) |
65: | `type: array, items: X` | `[X]` |
66: | In `required:` list | `T` |
67: | NOT in `required:` list | `Maybe T` |
68: 
69: ## Critical Rules
70: 
71: ### operationId
72: - Must be **kebab-case**: `create-my-feature` (becomes `createMyFeature` in Haskell)
73: - NOT PascalCase, NOT snake_case
74: 
75: ### Reserved words
76: - `_type` in YAML becomes `__type` in Haskell (double underscore)
77: - DB column mapping via `mapToDBKeys` strips the underscore back
78: 
79: ### Parameter order in Core.hs
80: Must match Servant route type exactly: path captures, then query params, then request body, then headers (in declaration order). All headers are `Maybe Text` even if marked required.
81: 
82: ### Enums
83: Always add `x-enum: true` on enum schemas. Without it, proper Haskell enum types with Beam/PostgreSQL instances won't be generated.
84: 
85: ```yaml
86: MyStatusEnum:
87:   type: string
88:   x-enum: true    # REQUIRED
89:   enum: [ACTIVE, INACTIVE]
90: ```
91: 
92: ### x-find / x-update
93: - `typename` must be Haskell types: `Text`, `Bool`, `Int`, `Scientific`, `Types.<EnumName>` — never `String`
94: - `isMaybe: true` is REQUIRED for nullable fields (not in `required:` list), otherwise type mismatch
95: - `isArray: true` generates `IN (...)` clause, pair with `returnsArray: true`
96: 
97: ### New DB table checklist
98: 1. Define schema in `doc/schemas/` with `x-find`/`x-update`
99: 2. Add to `doc/DBQueries.yaml`
100: 3. Add to `doc/Api.yaml` `components/schemas`
101: 4. Register in `src/Vayu/Types/Storage/BreezeDB.hs` (manual — add table to `BreezeDb` record + entity modification)
102: 5. Regenerate
103: 6. Forgetting step 4 = compiles but fails at runtime

105: ### New API endpoint checklist
106: 1. Define schema in `doc/schemas/`
107: 2. Define path in `doc/paths/`
108: 3. Add path reference to `doc/Api.yaml` (position matters for route ordering)
109: 4. Regenerate

119: ## Logging Rules
120: 
121: ### USE: One-line wrappers from `Vayu.Product.Logger`
122: 
123: ```haskell
124: import qualified Vayu.Product.Logger as ProductLogger
125: 
126: -- API-facing product functions:
127: myFunction reqBody shopUrl =
128:   ProductLogger.withProductAPILogging "myFunction" Logger.POST url ["body" .= reqBody] $
129:     SomeService.doWork reqBody
130: 
131: -- Internal product helpers:
132: buildContext shopUrl =
133:   ProductLogger.withFunctionLogging "buildContext" ["shopUrl" .= shopUrl] $
134:     fetchAndValidate shopUrl
135: ```
136: 
137: ### DO NOT: Use manual 2-line logging pairs
138: ```haskell
139: -- WRONG — legacy pattern, do not write new code like this
140: startTimestamp <- Logger.logProductAPIRequest "fn" Logger.POST url ["body" .= req]
141: result <- Service.doWork req
142: Logger.logProductAPIResponse "fn" startTimestamp result
143: ```
144: 
145: ### DO NOT: Add scattered logInfo/logDebug calls
146: ```haskell
147: -- WRONG — LLMs frequently do this
148: Logger.logInfo "myFunction" ["starting processing" .= True]
149: Logger.logInfo "myFunction" ["step 2 done" .= True]
150: Logger.logInfo "myFunction" ["returning result" .= True]
151: ```
152: 
153: Three logging levels cover everything: Product API (`withProductAPILogging`), Product Function (`withFunctionLogging`), and External API (in Services/External). No additional `logInfo` calls needed.

2: 
3: ## What is Vayu?
4: 
5: Vayu is a **Haskell backend** (Servant framework, Beam ORM, PostgreSQL) for Breeze - a checkout/payment platform. The majority of boilerplate code (types, API routes, DB queries, network calls, SQL schemas) is **auto-generated** from OpenAPI 3.0 YAML specifications using [OpenAPI Generator CLI v5.4.0](https://openapi-generator.tech/) with custom Mustache templates.
6: 
7: ## Why This Guide Exists
8: 
9: LLMs frequently introduce structural errors when generating code for this repo because they don't understand:
10: 1. Which files are generated vs hand-written
11: 2. How YAML specs map to generated Haskell code
12: 3. The custom vendor extensions (`x-find`, `x-update`, `x-schemas`, etc.)
13: 4. The separation between Common types, Storage types, Queries, and Network Calls
14: 5. The boundary: generated code stops at `Core.hs` - everything after is hand-written
15: 6. The layered architecture: Product orchestrates, Services/Internal owns domain logic
16: 7. The logging discipline: use wrappers, not scattered logInfo calls
17: 
18: ## The Golden Rule
19: 
20: > **NEVER manually edit files under `src/Vayu/Generated/`.** All changes to generated code must be made in the YAML specs or Mustache templates, then regenerated.

1: # Product Layer Architecture
2: 
3: ## Role
4: 
5: Product is the **orchestration layer**. It links multiple services/domains together for a single API flow. It should NOT contain standalone business logic for a single domain — that belongs in `Services/Internal`.
6: 
7: ```
8: Core.hs → flowWithTrace (context setup, no logging)
9:   → AuthMiddleware (optional)
10:     → Product.*.Main (orchestration + logging)
11:       → Services/Internal.* (single-domain business logic, queries)
12:       → Services/External.* (external API calls)
13: ```
14: 
15: ### What belongs in Product:
16: - Linking Cart + Customer + Shipping for a checkout flow
17: - Coordinating Order + Payment + Platform for order completion
18: - Request/response logging via `withProductAPILogging`
19: - Input validation before delegating to services
20: - Type conversion (Storage → Common) before returning
21: 
22: ### What does NOT belong in Product:
23: - Single-domain computations (e.g., pure order calculations → `Services/Internal/Order`)
24: - Direct DB queries (→ `Generated/Queries` exported through `Services/Internal`)
25: - Direct Redis access (→ should go through service layer)
26: - `logInfo` / `logDebug` scattered through the function body
27: 
28: ## Directory Structure
29: 
30: ```
31: src/Vayu/Product/              (48 domains, ~211 files)
32: ├── Cart/
33: │   ├── Main.hs                (entry point, exported to Core.hs)

35: │   ├── Utils.hs               (product-level helpers)

55: ### Naming conventions

61: ## Core.hs → Product Routing

63: ### flowWithTrace (Core.hs:4423-4440)
64: 
65: Every Core.hs handler calls `flowWithTrace` which:
66: 1. Generates UUIDs for missing sessionId, requestId, deviceId
67: 2. Parses testingMode from string to Bool
68: 3. Calls `RouteUtils.toFlowHandlerWithEnv` which injects context into FlowMonad and sets up a per-request log counter
69: 
70: **Core.hs does NOT log requests/responses. This is intentional.** All API logging happens in the Product layer.
71: 
72: ### Handler patterns in Core.hs
73: 
74: ```haskell
75: -- Pattern 1: Direct Product call (no auth)
76: getHeartBeat = flowWithTrace HeartBeat.heartBeat Nothing Nothing Nothing Nothing Nothing
77: 
78: -- Pattern 2: User auth → Product
79: getAddresses enforcedPostalCode accessToken =
80:   flowWithTrace $
81:     AuthMiddleware.validateAuth
82:       (APICommons.TokenFlows (Address.fetchAddresses enforcedPostalCode) Nothing)
83:       accessToken
84: 
85: -- Pattern 3: S2S auth with permission → Product
86: forceExecuteMandate reqBody accessToken =
87:   flowWithTrace $
88:     AuthMiddleware.validateS2SAuth accessToken WRITE MANDATES
89:       >>= UtilsCommon.handleBoolWithException
90:       >> Subscription.forceExecuteMandate reqBody

93: ## Logging — The Correct Pattern
94: 
95: ### USE: Product/Logger.hs wrappers (single-line)
96: 
97: ```haskell
98: import qualified Vayu.Product.Logger as ProductLogger
99: 
100: -- For API-facing product functions:
101: createCart reqBody shopUrl =
102:   ProductLogger.withProductAPILogging "createCart" Logger.POST url ["body" .= reqBody, "shopUrl" .= shopUrl] $
103:     CartService.create reqBody
104: 
105: -- For internal product functions:
106: buildContext reqBody shopUrl =
107:   ProductLogger.withFunctionLogging "buildContext" ["shopUrl" .= shopUrl] $
108:     fetchShop shopUrl >>= validate
109: ```
110: 
111: ### DO NOT USE: Manual 2-line pairs
112: 
113: ```haskell
114: -- OLD — do not write new code like this
115: startTimestamp <- Logger.logProductAPIRequest "createCart" Logger.POST url ["body" .= reqBody]
116: CartService.create reqBody
117:   >>= Logger.logProductAPIResponse "createCart" startTimestamp
118: ```
119: 
120: ### DO NOT USE: Scattered logInfo calls
121: 
122: ```haskell
123: -- WRONG — LLMs frequently add these
124: myFunction req = do
125:   Logger.logInfo "myFunction" ["starting" .= True]        -- NO
126:   result <- Service.doThing req
127:   Logger.logInfo "myFunction" ["result" .= result]         -- NO
128:   Logger.logInfo "myFunction" ["returning" .= True]        -- NO
129:   return result
130: ```

132: ### Three logging levels in the codebase
133: 
134: | Level | Wrapper | Where used | What it logs |
135: |-------|---------|------------|--------------|
136: | Product API | `withProductAPILogging` | Product Main.hs functions called by Core.hs | Request params + response + timing |
137: | Product Function | `withFunctionLogging` | Internal product helpers | Input args + return value |
138: | External API | (covered in external services doc) | Services/External | HTTP request + response + timing |
139: 
140: These three levels together provide full observability. No additional `logInfo` calls should be needed.

1: # Platform Service Layer
2: 
3: ## What Platform Service Is
4: 
5: Platform is the **central dispatch bridge** between Breeze's domain logic and e-commerce platform APIs. Every operation that touches a merchant's store (create cart, create order, check inventory, sync customer) goes through this layer, which routes to the correct platform-specific external service based on `ShopType`.
6: 
7: ## Supported Platforms (7)
8: 
9: | Platform | ShopType Enum | Maturity | External Subdirs | Key Capabilities |
10: |----------|--------------|----------|-----------------|------------------|
11: | Shopify | `ShopType_SHOPIFY` | Full | 35 | Cart, orders, inventory, webhooks, GQL, payments, subscriptions, StoreFront |
12: | WooCommerce | `ShopType_WOOCOMMERCE` | High | 15 | Orders, sessions, inventory, coupons, tracking, subscriptions |
13: | Magento | `ShopType_MAGENTO` | High | 17 | Cart, orders, inventory, invoices, addresses, customer, wallet |
14: | VTEX | `ShopType_VTEX` | Medium | 9 | Orders, payment provider (VTEX Payments) |
15: | CS-Cart | `ShopType_CSCART` | Basic | 11 | Cart sessions, customers, coupons, addresses |
16: | PrestaShop | `ShopType_PRESTASHOP` | Minimal | 2 | Order locking, sessions |
17: | Independent | `ShopType_INDEPENDENT` | Endpoint-based | 10 | Generic via shop_endpoints config |

65:     Types.ShopType_WOOCOMMERCE  -> WooCommerceInventory.checkItemsInInventory ...

129: ## DB Access Rule: One Read, One Update Per Table Per API
130: 
131: ### The Rule
132: 
133: In any single API flow (from Core.hs handler entry to response), each DB table should be:
134: - **Read at most once** — fetch at the entry point, thread through the call chain
135: - **Updated at most once** — collect all mutations, apply in one write
136: 
137: ### Why This Matters
138: 
139: - Each DB call adds ~2-5ms network latency
140: - Redundant reads compound in high-traffic flows (cart fetch, order creation)
141: - Shop table has caching which masks some cost, but order/cart/offer tables do not
142: - Webhook flows are latency-sensitive — redundant reads directly impact processing time
143: 
144: ### Anti-Pattern: Functions Take IDs Instead of Objects
145: 
146: ```haskell
147: -- WRONG: Each function fetches what it needs independently
148: fetchCartWithId cartId = do
149:   cart <- Cart.findCartWithId cartId
150:   shop <- Shop.findWithId (cart ^. shopId)       -- fetch #1
151:   ...
152:   returnFetchSuccess cart shopId                  -- calls Shop.findWithId again (fetch #2)
153: 
154: -- RIGHT: Fetch once, thread through
155: fetchCartWithId cartId = do
156:   cart <- Cart.findCartWithId cartId
157:   shop <- Shop.findWithId (cart ^. shopId)       -- fetch once
158:   ...
159:   returnFetchSuccess cart shop                   -- pass the object, not the ID
160: ```
161: 
162: ### Known Redundancies (DO NOT REFACTOR YET — phase this with QA)
163: 
164: | Flow | Table | What Happens | Where |
165: |------|-------|-------------|-------|
166: | `fetchCartWithId` → `returnFetchSuccess` | Shop | Shop fetched twice — parent has it, child re-fetches by ID | `Product/Cart/Main.hs` |
167: | `updateOrderStatusByWebhook` | Shop | Shop fetched up to 3x in different branches | `Product/Order/Main.hs` |
168: | `getOrCreateOrderWithAddress` | Order | Order potentially re-fetched after find | `Services/Internal/Order/Main.hs` |
169: | `createCart` (Product) | Shop | 11+ service calls, shop not threaded through | `Product/Cart/Main.hs` |
170: | `applyShipping` path | Offer | Offers re-processed instead of cached from earlier fetch | `Services/Internal/Cart/Main.hs` |
171: 
172: ### Refactoring Strategy (Phased — Requires QA)
173: 
174: **Phase 1: Shop threading** (lowest risk, highest impact)
175: - Shop is the most commonly re-fetched object
176: - Already cached, so functional impact is low but still wastes cache lookups
177: - Change function signatures to accept `Shop` instead of `ShopId` where the caller already has it
178: 
179: **Phase 2: Cart/Order threading** (medium risk)

3: ## What the Payment Domain Does
4: 
5: The Payment domain handles everything from the moment a customer clicks "Pay" to when the payment is confirmed or fails. It builds payment SDK payloads, manages payment method resolution, orchestrates Custom Payment Options (CPO), handles partial payments, verifies payment attempts, and integrates with the Euler/JusPay payment gateway.

92: ## Flow 2: HyperPay SDK Payload (The Core of Payment)
93: 
94: `Services/Internal/Payment/HyperPay.createPaymentDetails` is the heart of payment — it builds the encrypted SDK payload that the frontend sends to Euler/JusPay.
95: 
96: ```
97: createPaymentDetails(shop, order, cart, customer, addresses, offers, merchant, shippingRule, subscriptionPlan, cpoContext)
98:   ↓
99: 1. Customer Validation
100:    ├── Sanitize customer name (Euler requires valid names)
101:    ├── Async update Euler customer if name was invalid
102:    └── Check customer-based locking eligibility
103:   ↓
104: 2. Build SDK Payload (mkPaymentPayloadObject)
105:    ├── OrderDetails JSON: order_id, amount, customer, basket
106:    ├── Platform cart data (if applicable)
107:    ├── Subscription mandate details (if subscription)
108:    └── Serialize & sign with merchant key (HMAC-SHA256)
109:   ↓
110: 3. Payment Locking Payload (getPaymentLockingPayload)
111:    ├── Lock payment methods based on shipping rules
112:    ├── Lock COD for specific customers
113:    ├── Add mandate payment method filters
114:    ├── Add RTO-based locking
115:    └── Add CPO-based locking (for combined payment options)
116:   ↓
117: 4. Actions (determines payload type)
118:    ├── Initiate: full order details for new payment
119:    ├── PaymentPage: resume existing payment
120:    └── UpdateOrder: order update without full recreation
121:   ↓
122: Output: PaymentDetails { requestId, service="in.juspay.hyperpay", payload, signature }
123: ```

125: ### Payment Locking
126: 
127: Payment locking restricts which payment methods are available based on rules:
128: 
129: | Lock Source | What It Locks | Where Configured |
130: |------------|---------------|------------------|
131: | Shipping Rule | Methods not allowed for the selected shipping zone | `ShippingRule.paymentMethodGroupPreferenceIndex` |
132: | Customer Lock | COD locked for flagged customers | Customer attributes |
133: | RTO Lock | COD locked for high-return addresses | RTO service |
134: | Mandate Lock | Non-mandate methods locked for subscriptions | Subscription config |
135: | CPO Lock | Methods incompatible with applied CPO | CPO provider config |
136: 
137: ## Flow 3: Payment Attempt Verification
138: 
139: When the frontend completes payment collection via Euler SDK, it calls back to verify.
140: 
141: ```
142: POST /session/payment-attempt
143:   ↓
144: Product/Payment/PaymentAttempt.verifyPaymentAttempt
145:   ├── Check order/payment already succeeded (prevent double-processing)
146:   ├── Cache delivery items grouping preference
147:   ├── Update order: device_id, transaction_id, payment_method

149:   └── Return: PaymentAttemptResponse

151:        ├── resumePaymentPayload: signed SDK payload (if resuming failed payment)
152:        ├── offers: applied offers
153:        └── matrixResponse: optional Matrix Router response
154: ```

157: 
158: For failed/abandoned payments, a `ResumePaymentInnerPayload` is built:
159: - `action: "resumePayment"`
160: - `txnReference: original attempt reference`
161: - `orderDetails: encrypted original order details`
162: - `signature: HMAC-SHA256 signed`

264: 
265: | Euler Status | Breeze OrderStatus | Notes |
266: |-------------|-------------------|-------|
267: | `CHARGED` | `SUCCESS` (or `PARTIALLY_PAID` if PPR) | Payment complete |

271: | `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` | `FAILED` | Auth passed, gateway rejected |

1: # Order Lifecycle
2: 
3: ## What the Order Domain Does
4: 
5: The Order domain manages the complete lifecycle of an order: creation after payment initiation, status resolution via the Euler gateway, platform order creation on the merchant's e-commerce store, webhook processing for status updates, COD-to-prepaid conversion, and refund orchestration. It ties together payment completion with platform fulfillment.
6: 
7: ## Architecture
8: 
9: ```
10: Core.hs (route handlers)
11:   ↓
12: Product/Order/              ← orchestration (5 modules)
13:   ├── Main.hs              — public API: getOrderWithId, orderRefundWebhook, orderStatusSync
14:   ├── Workflow.hs          — ProcessTracker workflows: orderStatusWorkflow, createPlatformOrderWorkflow
15:   ├── Utils.hs             — private: createPlatformOrder, getOrderAndPaymentDetails
16:   ├── CODToPrepaid/Main.hs — COD to prepaid conversion
17:   └── Types.hs             — workflow tracking data types
18: Product/Refund/             ← refund orchestration (2 modules)
19:   ├── Main.hs
20:   └── Utils.hs
21:   ↓
22: Services/Internal/Order/    ← domain logic (6 modules)
23:   ├── Main.hs              — order creation/retrieval
24:   ├── Queries.hs           — DB queries (findWithId, updateStatusByIdEither)
25:   ├── Refund/
26:   │   ├── Main.hs          — refund webhook processing
27:   │   ├── Transaction.hs   — refund transaction handling
28:   │   └── Context.hs       — refund context creation
29:   └── Utils.hs
30: Services/Internal/Platform/Order.hs — dispatch bridge (ShopType × OrderStatus)
31:   ↓
32: Services/External/          ← platform-specific order creation
33:   ├── Shopify/Order/Main.hs
34:   ├── WooCommerce/Order.hs
35:   ├── Magento/Order.hs
36:   ├── Vtex/Order.hs
37:   ├── CsCart/Order.hs
38:   ├── Presta/Order.hs
39:   ├── IndependentShop/Order.hs
40:   └── Order/Refund/         ← refund handlers per platform
41:       ├── Main.hs           — handler dispatch
42:       ├── Shopify.hs
43:       ├── WooCommerce.hs
44:       └── Magento.hs
45: ```
46: 
47: ## Order Lifecycle States
48: 
49: ```
50: CREATED ──→ PENDING ──→ SUCCESS ──→ PLATFORM_ORDER_CREATED
51:                     ├──→ PARTIALLY_PAID ──→ PLATFORM_ORDER_CREATED
52:                     ├──→ FAILED
53:                     ├──→ AUTO_REFUNDED
54:                     └──→ AUTO_CANCELLED
55: ```
56: 
57: | Status | Meaning | What Happens Next |
58: |--------|---------|-------------------|
59: | `CREATED` | Order record exists, payment not started | Wait for payment initiation |
60: | `PENDING` | Payment in progress (Euler processing) | Poll/webhook for resolution |
61: | `SUCCESS` | Full payment received (or COD confirmed) | Create platform order |
62: | `PARTIALLY_PAID` | Partial payment via PPR | Create platform order (with partial amount) |
63: | `FAILED` | Payment failed | Refund gift cards, mark abandoned |
64: | `AUTO_REFUNDED` | Gateway auto-refunded (timeout) | No platform order |
65: | `AUTO_CANCELLED` | Abandoned after max retries | Trigger abandonment flow |
66: 
67: ## Phase 1: Order Status Resolution (CREATED/PENDING → SUCCESS/FAILED)
68: 
69: **Entry:** `Product/Order/Main.getOrderWithId(orderId, isSyncOrderFlow)`
70: 
71: ```
72: getOrderWithId
73:   ├── Fetch order from DB
74:   ├── Determine payment source:
75:   │    ├── Regular (Euler): getOrderAndPaymentDetails
76:   │    │    └── checkOrderStatus → requestEulerOrder (Euler API)
77:   │    ├── CPO-only: CPOService.getCustomPaymentTransactionDetails
78:   │    ├── Matrix: checkMatrixOrderStatus
79:   │    └── CO_COD (Shopify Payments COD): always SUCCESS + CASH method
80:   ├── Map Euler status → Breeze OrderStatus
81:   └── Return: (updatedOrder, OrderAndPaymentDetails)
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Status Mapping (Euler → Breeze)
85: 
86: | Euler Status | Breeze Status |
87: |-------------|---------------|
88: | `CHARGED` | `SUCCESS` (or `PARTIALLY_PAID` if PPR active) |
89: | `COD_INITIATED` | `SUCCESS` |
90: | `NEW` / `PENDING_VBV` / `AUTHORIZING` | `PENDING` |
91: | `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` | `FAILED` |
92: | `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` | `FAILED` |
93: | `JUSPAY_DECLINED` | `FAILED` |
94: | `AUTO_REFUNDED` | `REFUNDED` |
95: 
96: ### Order Source Types
97: 
98: | Source | Meaning | Status Flow |
99: |--------|---------|-------------|
100: | `null` | Regular Euler payment | Standard flow |
101: | `"CO"` | Shopify Payments (prepaid) | Euler → ShopifyPayments order |
102: | `"CO_COD"` | Shopify Payments (COD) | Always SUCCESS, CASH method |
103: 
104: ## Phase 2: Platform Order Creation (SUCCESS → Platform Order)
105: 
106: Once payment is confirmed, the order is created on the merchant's e-commerce platform.
107: 
108: ### Synchronous Path
109: 
110: ```
111: Product/Order/Utils.createPlatformOrder((order, orderAndPaymentDetails))
112:   ├── 1. Fetch context: shop, cart, customer, addresses, offers, shipping provider, GST
113:   ├── 2. Check if Shopify Payments (source == "CO" or "CO_COD")
114:   │     └── Yes: ShopifyPaymentsOrderService.findOrCreateAndStoreShopifyPaymentWithLock
115:   ├── 3. Dispatch by (ShopType × OrderStatus):
116:   │     └── Platform/Order.findOrCreateOrder (see dispatch matrix below)
117:   ├── 4. If FAILED: refund gift cards
118:   └── 5. Return: OrderWithPlatformOrderResponse
119: ```
120: 
121: ### Asynchronous Path (ProcessTracker Workflow)
122: 
123: ```
124: Product/Order/Workflow.createPlatformOrderWorkflow(ProcessTracker task)
125:   ├── Extract PlatformOrderWorkflowTrackingData from task
126:   ├── Check if order source is blocked (CO_COD blocked by default)
127:   ├── Call createPlatformOrderRecon → createPlatformOrder
128:   ├── On failure: reschedule with exponential backoff (up to maxRetries)
129:   ├── On success: mark workflow FINISHED
130:   └── On max retries exceeded: auto-cancel order + create abandonment task
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Platform Dispatch Matrix (Services/Internal/Platform/Order.hs)
134: 
135: The `findOrCreateOrder` function is a compound switch on `(OrderStatus, ShopType)`:
136: 
137: ```haskell
138: findOrCreateOrder customer shop cart order ... =
139:   case (latestOrderStatus, shop ^. Shop._type) of
140:     (SUCCESS, SHOPIFY)          → Shopify.findOrCreateOrder
141:     (PARTIALLY_PAID, SHOPIFY)   → Shopify.findOrCreateOrder
142:     (SUCCESS, WOOCOMMERCE)      → WooCommerce.createOrder
143:     (PARTIALLY_PAID, WOOCOMMERCE) → WooCommerce.createOrder
144:     (SUCCESS, MAGENTO)          → Magento.createOrder
145:     (PARTIALLY_PAID, MAGENTO)   → Magento.createOrder

171: Two ProcessTracker workflows run in sequence:

230: 
231: ```

233:   ├── Find order by ID

1: # ProcessTracker — Distributed Task Scheduler
2: 
3: ## What ProcessTracker Does
4: 
5: ProcessTracker is a distributed, database-backed task scheduler that manages all asynchronous workflows in Vayu. It handles order status polling, platform order creation, abandoned cart notifications, analytics aggregation, campaign scheduling, product sync, and more. The system is built on three logical components: **Producer** (fetches and dispatches tasks), **Consumer** (executes workflow handlers), and **Cleaner** (implicit — terminal statuses + time-window filtering naturally age out completed tasks).
6: 
7: ## Architecture Overview
8: 
9: ```
10: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
11: │                        ProcessTracker Table (PostgreSQL)            │
12: │  id | runner | retryCount | scheduleTime | trackingData | status   │
13: └────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────┘
14:          │ SELECT WHERE status IN (NEW, PENDING)            │ UPDATE status, retryCount,
15:          │ AND scheduleTime IN [lowerLimit, upperLimit]     │ scheduleTime
16:          ▼                                                  │
17: ┌─────────────────┐    HTTP POST /process-tracker/consumer  │
18: │    PRODUCER      │ ──────────────────────────────────────► │
19: │  (infinite loop) │    ProcessTrackerBatch { ptList }      │
20: │                  │                                        │
21: │  Redis lock:     │                              ┌─────────┴─────────┐
22: │  PRODUCER_LOCK   │                              │     CONSUMER       │
23: └─────────────────┘                              │  (HTTP endpoint)   │
24:                                                   │                    │
25:                                                   │  Per-task:         │
26:                                                   │  1. Redis lock     │
27:                                                   │  2. PROCESS_STARTED│
28:                                                   │  3. runWorkflow()  │
29:                                                   │  4. Update PT state│
30:                                                   │  5. Release lock   │
31:                                                   └────────────────────┘
32: ```
33: 
34: ### Deployment Model
35: 
36: Producer and Consumer run in **separate Vayu instances**:
37: 
38: - **Producer instance**: `ENABLE_PROCESS_TRACKER=true` + `PRODUCER_ENABLED=true` — runs the infinite producer loop instead of the HTTP server
39: - **Consumer instance**: Standard Vayu HTTP server — exposes `POST /process-tracker/consumer` endpoint
40: - Producer calls Consumer via HTTP (with S2S auth token), through a load balancer for horizontal scaling
41: 
42: ```
43: App.hs:
44:   if isPTFlow
45:     then ProcessTracker.startProcessTracker   ← Producer mode (no HTTP server)
46:     else runSettings settings =<< runVayuApp  ← Consumer/API mode (HTTP server)
47: ```
48: 
49: ## Data Model
50: 
51: ### ProcessTracker Table
52: 
53: ```sql
54: CREATE TABLE public."processTracker" (
55:   "id"              VARCHAR(8192) NOT NULL,    -- Deterministic task ID (idempotency key)
56:   "runner"          VARCHAR(8192) NOT NULL,    -- RunnerEnum: workflow type
57:   "retryCount"      INTEGER       NOT NULL,    -- Current retry attempt
58:   "scheduleTime"    TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL,    -- When to execute (UTC)
59:   "trackingData"    JSON          NOT NULL,    -- Workflow-specific context
60:   "businessStatus"  VARCHAR(8192) NOT NULL,    -- PENDING | FAILED | SUCCESS
61:   "status"          VARCHAR(8192) NOT NULL,    -- PT lifecycle state
62:   "createdAt"       TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL,
63:   "updatedAt"       TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL
64: );
65: ```
66: 
67: ### Task Lifecycle States (PTStatuses)
68: 
69: ```
70:      ┌──── NEW ◄─────────────────────────────────── Task created
71:      │
72:      ▼
73:   PENDING ◄──── Workflow returns PENDING + timeOffset ── Retry scheduled
74:      │
75:      ▼
76:   PROCESS_STARTED ──── Consumer acquired lock, executing workflow
77:      │
78:      ├──► FINISHED   ── Workflow succeeded, no more retries
79:      ├──► CANCELLED  ── Max retries exceeded / unsupported runner / manual cancel
80:      └──► PENDING    ── Workflow failed or needs retry → reschedule
81: ```
82: 
83: | Status | Meaning | Next Action |
84: |--------|---------|-------------|
85: | `NEW` | Just created, awaiting pickup | Producer fetches it |
86: | `PENDING` | Awaiting retry after previous attempt | Producer re-fetches when scheduleTime arrives |
87: | `PROCESS_STARTED` | Consumer acquired lock, executing | Wait for workflow completion |
88: | `FINISHED` | Workflow succeeded | Terminal — no further processing |
89: | `CANCELLED` | Terminated (max retries, manual, unsupported) | Terminal — no further processing |
90: | `ABORTED` | Reserved but unused in practice | Terminal |
91: 
92: ### Business Statuses
93: 
94: Separate from PT status — tracks the business outcome independently:
95: - `PENDING` — default on creation
96: - `SUCCESS` — business operation succeeded
97: - `FAILED` — business operation failed

99: ## Component 1: Producer
100: 
101: **File**: `src/Vayu/Product/ProcessTracker/Producer.hs`
102: 
103: The Producer is an infinite loop that fetches eligible tasks from the database and sends them to the Consumer via HTTP.
104: 
105: ### Producer Flow
106: 
107: ```
108: startProducer(mutexFlag)
109:   │
110:   ▼
111: producerLooper(mutexFlag)                    ← forever loop
112:   │
113:   ├── Check mutexFlag (SIGINT/SIGTERM?)      ← graceful shutdown
114:   ├── Spawn thread: producerFlowOps
115:   │     │
116:   │     ├── Log timing, detect delays
117:   │     └── producerFlow:
118:   │           │
119:   │           ├── 1. Calculate time window:
120:   │           │      upperLimit = now - SCHEDULER_LOWER_LIMIT (default: 0s)
121:   │           │      lowerLimit = now - (SCHEDULER_LOWER_LIMIT + SCHEDULER_UPPER_LIMIT) (default: 1800s)
122:   │           │
123:   │           ├── 2. Acquire Redis lock: PRODUCER_LOCK (TTL: PRODUCER_TTL)
124:   │           │      └── If lock held by another instance → skip this iteration
125:   │           │
126:   │           ├── 3. Fetch tasks:
127:   │           │      SELECT * FROM processTracker
128:   │           │        WHERE status IN ('NEW', 'PENDING')
129:   │           │        AND scheduleTime BETWEEN lowerLimit AND upperLimit
130:   │           │
131:   │           ├── 4. Batch tasks (PRODUCER_BATCH_SIZE, default: 5)
132:   │           │      └── Each batch wrapped in ProcessTrackerBatch { id, ptList, ... }
133:   │           │
134:   │           └── 5. POST each batch to Consumer:
135:   │                  {consumerEndpoint}/process-tracker/consumer
136:   │                  Headers: X-S2s-Token, X-Session-Id
137:   │
138:   └── Sleep: SCHEDULER_SLEEP_TIME ms (default: 10,000ms = 10s)
139: ```
140: 
141: ### Time Window Explained
142: 
143: The producer only fetches tasks whose `scheduleTime` falls within a sliding window:
144: 
145: ```
146:                     lowerLimit                upperLimit
147:                        │                         │
148:   ─────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┼──── now
149:         too old        │    eligible window       │  too new
150:     (already picked    │   (producer fetches)     │  (not yet due)
151:      or abandoned)     │                          │
152: ```
153: 
154: - `upperLimit = now - SCHEDULER_LOWER_LIMIT` (default 0s → tasks due now)
155: - `lowerLimit = now - (SCHEDULER_LOWER_LIMIT + SCHEDULER_UPPER_LIMIT)` (default 1800s → up to 30 min old)
156: 
157: Tasks older than the window are never re-fetched — this is the **implicit cleaner** mechanism. Tasks that reach terminal status (FINISHED/CANCELLED) also have their status changed, so they're excluded from the `NEW`/`PENDING` filter.
158: 
159: ### Redis Lock (Producer-Level)
160: 
161: Only one producer instance processes tasks at a time:
162: - Lock key: `PRODUCER_LOCK` (configurable)
163: - TTL: `PRODUCER_TTL` seconds (default: 1000)
164: - Acquired via `SET IF NOT EXISTS`
165: - Released after batch dispatch completes
166: - Auto-expires on crash (TTL)
167: 
168: ## Component 2: Consumer
169: 
170: **File**: `src/Vayu/Product/ProcessTracker/Consumer.hs`
171: 
172: The Consumer receives batches via HTTP and executes each task's workflow handler.
173: 
174: ### Consumer Flow
175: 
176: ```
177: POST /process-tracker/consumer  (ProcessTrackerBatch)
178:   │
179:   ▼
180: consumer(batch)
181:   │
182:   ├── Log batch request
183:   ├── handleTasks(batch.ptList):
184:   │     │
185:   │     └── For each task:
186:   │           │
187:   │           ├── 1. Extract cartId from trackingData (if present)
188:   │           ├── 2. Resolve session from cart → override Flow environment
189:   │           ├── 3. Spawn thread with new session context:
190:   │           │
191:   │           │     executePTTaskWithLock(task):
192:   │           │       │
193:   │           │       ├── bracket pattern:
194:   │           │       │   Setup:   setConsumerLock("pt:consumer:{taskId}", TTL)
195:   │           │       │   Action:  executePTTask(task, isLockAcquired)
196:   │           │       │   Cleanup: removeConsumerLock("pt:consumer:{taskId}")
197:   │           │       │
198:   │           │       └── executePTTask:
199:   │           │             │
200:   │           │             ├── If lock NOT acquired → skip (already running elsewhere)
201:   │           │             │
202:   │           │             ├── If lock acquired:
203:   │           │             │   ├── Update status → PROCESS_STARTED
204:   │           │             │   ├── spawnThreadAwait → runWorkflow(task)
205:   │           │             │   ├── Receive WorkFlowResponse:
206:   │           │             │   │     { ptState, timeOffset, cascadingTask }
207:   │           │             │   ├── updateNextPTState(id, retryCount+1, newScheduleTime, response)
208:   │           │             │   └── If cascadingTask present → insert it
209:   │           │             │
210:   │           │             └── If thread fails:
211:   │           │                   └── Default: PENDING + 200s offset (retry later)
212:   │           │
213:   │           └── Continue with next task
214:   │
215:   └── Return: PTConsumerAcknowledgement { status: SUCCESS, id: batchId }
216: ```
217: 
218: ### Redis Lock (Task-Level)
219: 
220: Prevents parallel execution of the same task across consumer instances:
221: - Lock key: `pt:consumer:{taskId}`
222: - TTL: `PT_TASK_PROCESSING_TTL` seconds (default: 150)
223: - If lock exists → silently skip (another consumer is processing it)
224: - Released in cleanup (bracket pattern) — even on exceptions
225:

261: ### WorkFlowResponse Contract
262: 
263: Every workflow handler returns:
264: 
265: ```haskell
266: data WorkFlowResponse = WorkFlowResponse
267:   { _ptState       :: PTStatuses              -- Next PT status
268:   , _timeOffset    :: Int                     -- Seconds to delay before next retry
269:   , _cascadingTask :: Maybe ProcessTracker    -- Optional follow-up task to create
270:   }
271: ```
272: 
273: | Return Pattern | Meaning |
274: |----------------|---------|
275: | `FINISHED, 0, Nothing` | Success — task complete |
276: | `PENDING, N, Nothing` | Retry in N seconds |
277: | `CANCELLED, 0, Nothing` | Give up — no more retries |
278: | `FINISHED, 0, Just task` | Success + spawn follow-up task |
279: | `PENDING, N, Just task` | Retry + also spawn follow-up task |
280: 
281: ### State Update Logic
282: 
283: ```
284: updateNextPTState(taskId, retryCount+1, rescheduledTime, workflowResponse):
285:   │
286:   ├── rescheduledTime = scheduleTime + timeOffset
287:   ├── UPDATE processTracker SET status=ptState, retryCount=new, scheduleTime=rescheduled
288:   └── If cascadingTask present → INSERT new task row
289: ```

291: ## Component 3: Cleaner (Implicit)
292: 
293: Unlike traditional schedulers, ProcessTracker does **not** have an explicit cleaner process. Instead, cleanup is achieved through three implicit mechanisms:
294: 
295: ### 1. Terminal Statuses
296: 
297: Tasks reaching `FINISHED`, `CANCELLED`, or `ABORTED` are never re-fetched because the producer only queries `status IN ('NEW', 'PENDING')`.
298: 
299: ### 2. Time-Window Filtering
300: 
301: The producer's sliding time window (`now - upperLimit` to `now - lowerLimit`) naturally excludes:
302: - Tasks too far in the past (older than `SCHEDULER_LOWER_LIMIT + SCHEDULER_UPPER_LIMIT` seconds)
303: - Tasks scheduled for the future (not yet due)
304: 
305: Old PENDING tasks that fall outside the window are effectively abandoned — they remain in the database but are never picked up again.
306: 
307: ### 3. Max Retry Termination
308: 
309: Each workflow checks `retryCount >= maxRetries` and returns `CANCELLED` when exceeded, preventing infinite retries:
310: 
311: ```haskell
312: -- Example from orderStatusWorkflow:
313: if retryCount >= ShopUtils.getMaxRetries mOrderStatusReconConfig
314:   then do
315:     autoCancelBzOrderAndCreateAbandonmentCheckoutTask ...
316:     pure cancelledWorkflowResponse
317:   else ...
318: ```
319: 
320: ### Note: No Row Deletion
321: 
322: Completed tasks are **never deleted** from the database. They accumulate over time with terminal statuses. This provides audit trail and debugging capability but means the `processTracker` table grows unboundedly. Periodic database-level cleanup (e.g., cron job deleting FINISHED/CANCELLED tasks older than N days) would need to be done outside the application.

324: ## Retry & Backoff
325: 
326: ### RetryConfig (Per-Shop, Per-Workflow)
327: 
328: ```haskell
329: data RetryConfig = RetryConfig
330:   { _maxRetries    :: Int    -- Max attempts (default: 5)
331:   , _initialDelay  :: Int    -- Initial delay in minutes (default: 5)
332:   , _backoffFactor :: Int    -- Multiplicative factor (default: 2)
333:   }

336: ### Time Offset Calculation (Exponential Backoff)
337: 
338: ```haskell
339: calculateTimeOffset config retryCount =
340:   (backoffFactor ^ (retryCount + 1)) * 60   -- Result in seconds
341: ```

343: With defaults (`backoffFactor=2`):
344: 
345: | Retry # | Offset (seconds) | Offset (human) |
346: |---------|-------------------|----------------|
347: | 0 | 2^1 × 60 = 120 | 2 min |
348: | 1 | 2^2 × 60 = 240 | 4 min |
349: | 2 | 2^3 × 60 = 480 | 8 min |
350: | 3 | 2^4 × 60 = 960 | 16 min |
351: | 4 | 2^5 × 60 = 1920 | 32 min |

436: ## Workflow State Lock
437: 
438: **File**: `src/Vayu/Product/ProcessTracker/Utils.hs`
439: 
440: Beyond task-level locks, workflows can acquire **state locks** to prevent concurrent modification of the same domain entity:
441: 
442: ```haskell
443: executeWorkflowWithStateLock :: Text -> Flow WorkFlowResponse -> Flow WorkFlowResponse
444: executeWorkflowWithStateLock stateKey workflow =
445:   bracket
446:     (setWorkflowLock stateKey)          -- Acquire: SET IF NOT EXISTS, TTL=workflowLockTTL
447:     (\_ -> removeWorkflowLock stateKey) -- Release: DELETE key
448:     (\isLocked ->
449:       if isLocked
450:         then workflow                   -- Execute workflow
451:         else pendingWorkflowResponse 300  -- Retry in 5 min
452:     )
453: ```
454: 
455: - Lock key pattern: e.g., `"state:cart:{cartId}"`, `"pt:recon-workflow:{cartId}"`
456: - TTL: `WORKFLOW_LOCK_TTL` seconds (default: 200)
457: - If lock unavailable → workflow returns PENDING with 300s offset (try again later)
458: 
459: ## Locking Summary
460: 
461: Three levels of distributed locking, each with a distinct purpose:
462: 
463: | Level | Redis Key Pattern | TTL | Purpose |
464: |-------|-------------------|-----|---------|
465: | **Producer** | `PRODUCER_LOCK` | `PRODUCER_TTL` (1000s) | Single-producer guarantee across instances |
466: | **Task** | `pt:consumer:{taskId}` | `PT_TASK_PROCESSING_TTL` (150s) | Prevent parallel execution of same task |
467: | **Workflow State** | `state:cart:{cartId}` etc. | `WORKFLOW_LOCK_TTL` (200s) | Prevent concurrent domain entity modification |

617: ## Key Design Patterns
618: 
619: ### Idempotency
620: - Deterministic task IDs prevent duplicates — scheduling the same order status check twice results in a DB unique constraint violation, which is treated as "already scheduled"
621: - Consumer Redis locks prevent parallel execution of the same task
622: 
623: ### Cascade Workflows
624: - A workflow can return a `cascadingTask` in its response
625: - Consumer automatically inserts the cascading task after the parent completes
626: - Enables multi-step orchestrations: order status check → platform order creation → abandonment
627: 
628: ### Session Preservation
629: - Consumer extracts `cartId` from tracking data
630: - Resolves session ID from cart → overrides Flow context
631: - Each task executes with the correct session scope, maintaining traceability
632: 
633: ### Graceful Degradation
634: - Unknown RunnerEnum fallback prevents crashes during rolling deployments
635: - Two-step query: try unfiltered first, fall back to known-enums-only filter
636: - Logs `UNKNOWN_RUNNER_ENUM_DETECTED` alert for monitoring

661: ### Missing Explicit Cleaner
662: - FINISHED/CANCELLED tasks accumulate in the database forever
663: - No periodic purge of old terminal-status tasks
664: - Table will grow unboundedly — recommend adding an external cron job to DELETE rows with terminal status older than N days

667: - `src/Vayu/Services/Internal/ProcessTracker/Queries.hs` suppresses incomplete pattern warnings — the `predicateWithFilter` function has a catch-all `predicateWithFilter filterBy pt = predicate filterBy pt` that delegates to the standard predicate, but not all `FilterBy` constructors have explicit `predicateWithFilter` cases
668: 
669: ### Producer Time Window Gap
670: - If a task's `scheduleTime` is pushed far into the future (e.g., backoff exceeds `SCHEDULER_UPPER_LIMIT`), it may fall outside the producer's window and never be picked up
671: - Mitigation: Ensure `SCHEDULER_UPPER_LIMIT` is large enough for the maximum possible backoff delay
672: 
673: ### No Consumer-Side Retry
674: - If the Producer's HTTP call to the Consumer fails, the batch is silently dropped
675: - Tasks remain in NEW/PENDING state and will be re-fetched in the next producer cycle (self-healing)
676: - But if the Consumer endpoint is persistently down, tasks pile up until the time window passes
677: 
678: ### Session Resolution
679: - Consumer resolves session from `cartId` in tracking data — workflows without a `cartId` field get a random session ID, which may limit traceability

162: ## Cart Lifecycle
163: 
164: ### 1. Cart Creation
165: 
166: ```
167: POST /cart  (CartRequestEnum: CreateCartRequest | UpdateCartRequest | ...)
168:   ↓
169: Product/Cart/Main.createCart
170:   ├── Parse request type (CreateCartRequest, UpdateCartRequest, etc.)
171:   ├── Validate subscription flow (if subscription cart)
172:   ├── Cart.createCartWithItemsAndOffers
173:   │     ├── Generate nanoid for cart ID
174:   │     ├── Create cart record in DB
175:   │     ├── Create cart items from request
176:   │     └── Create initial offers from request (platform discounts)
177:   ├── Platform.createCart (sync to Shopify/WooCommerce/etc.)
178:   ├── If PAYMENT journey: create payment session (HyperPay payload)
179:   ├── Handle free gifts (if shop config enables)
180:   ├── Spawn async: customer ingestion, campaign triggers
181:   └── Return: CartCreateResponse { cart, items, offers, paymentDetails }
182: ```

184: ### 2. Cart Fetch

187: GET /cart/{cartId}
188:   ↓
189: Product/Cart/Main.fetchCartWithId
190:   ├── JWT validation (optional)
191:   ├── Cart.findCartWithId (DB lookup)
192:   ├── CartItem.findCartItems (get items)
193:   ├── Offer.findOffersByCartId (get applied offers)
194:   ├── Build CartResponse { cart, items, offers }
195:   ├── If PAYMENT journey: create payment session

200: 
201: ```
202: PUT /cart/shipping
203:   ↓
204: Product/Cart/Main.updateCartWithShipping
205:   ├── Validate shipping rule
206:   ├── Cart.applyShipping (calculate charges, taxes)

210: ### 4. Cart Price Update Flow (when offers change)
211: 
212: ```
213: Any offer apply/remove
214:   → Offer.Utils.updatePriceAndCalculateTax
215:     ├── Recalculate totalDiscount from all active offers
216:     ├── Recalculate totalPrice = initialPrice - totalDiscount + shipping + tax + surcharge
217:     ├── Handle tax adjustment based on platform:
218:     │     ├── Shopify + CUSTOM_OFFERS issuer: preserve existing tax
219:     │     ├── Shopify + SHOP issuer: recalculate from checkout
220:     │     └── Other platforms: standard calculation
221:     └── Cart.Queries.updateCartWithDiscount (persist new prices)
222: ```
223: 
224: ## Offer System — Two Fundamentally Different Flows
225: 
226: There are **two completely different offer flows** that must not be confused. They differ in who applies the offer, when it hits the DB, and what the backend's role is.
227: 
228: | | Platform Offers | Euler/JusPay Offers |
229: |---|---|---|
230: | **What** | Shopify/WooCommerce/Magento discount codes | Payment-method-specific cashback (e.g., 10% off on HDFC cards) |
231: | **Who applies** | Breeze backend (via platform API) | Frontend (via Euler SDK) |
232: | **Backend role** | Full lifecycle: apply, remove, recalculate cart | List only — no apply/remove call from frontend |
233: | **When stored in DB** | Immediately on apply | Only AFTER payment succeeds at Euler |
234: | **Issuer in DB** | `SHOP` | `BREEZE` (with `issuerOfferId` = Euler offer ID) |
235: | **Cart updated** | Yes — prices recalculated immediately | No — cart unchanged until payment completes |
236: | **API** | `PUT /offer/{cartId}` | `POST /offer/list` |
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ### Flow 1: Platform Offers (PUT Offer)
241: 
242: Platform offers are discount codes from the merchant's e-commerce platform (Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, CsCart). When a customer enters a coupon code, Breeze calls the platform API to apply/remove it, then syncs the result to its own DB.
243: 
244: **The backend owns the full lifecycle: apply → update cart → store offer → return response.**
245: 
246: #### Entry Point
247: 
248: ```
249: PUT /offer/{cartId}  (operationId: put-offer)
250:   → Core.hs → putOffer
251:     → Product/Offer.putOffer
252: ```
253: 
254: Request body is `PUTOfferRequestEnum`:
255: - `PUTOfferRequest` — apply or remove a coupon code
256: - `RemoveFreeGiftRequest` — remove a free gift item
257: 
258: #### Apply Flow (step by step)
259: 
260: ```
261: Product/Offer.putOffer(cartId, PUTOfferRequest)
262:   ↓
263: handlePUTOfferRequest(cartId, reqBody)
264:   │
265:   ├── 1. Fetch context: cart, shop, cartItems, order, customer, addresses, CPO
266:   │
267:   ├── 2. Determine path by issuer (reqBody.sponsoredBy):
268:   │     ├── FREE_GIFT → handleFreeGiftOffer (special path)
269:   │     ├── GIFT_CARD → handlePlatformOffer(isGiftCard=True)
270:   │     └── SHOP/default:
271:   │           ├── Check feature flag: useBreezeOfferEngine?
272:   │           │     ├── YES → Breeze path (see below)
273:   │           │     └── NO  → Platform path (see below)
274:   │
275:   ├── 3a. PLATFORM PATH (traditional):
276:   │     ├── Platform/Offer.applyOffer (dispatch by ShopType)
277:   │     │     ├── SHOPIFY → Shopify.updateOffer
278:   │     │     │     └── StoreFrontCart.updateCartWithOfferOrGiftCard (GraphQL)
279:   │     │     │     └── Shopify validates code, returns updated checkout
280:   │     │     ├── WOOCOMMERCE → WooCommerce/Coupon.applyCoupon (REST)
281:   │     │     ├── MAGENTO → Magento/Coupon.applyCoupon (REST)
282:   │     │     └── CSCART → CsCart/Offer.update (REST)
283:   │     ├── Platform returns: UpdateOfferResponse { cart, offers }
284:   │     │     (cart prices come from the platform's calculation)
285:   │     └── Continue to step 4
286:   │
287:   │  3b. BREEZE PATH (newer — Breeze's own offer engine):
288:   │     ├── OfferCode.checkOfferEligibility (run JS eligibility rule)
289:   │     ├── OfferCode.calculateDiscount (run JS discount rule)
290:   │     ├── Offer.Main.applyOffer → create Offer record
291:   │     ├── Offer.Utils.updatePriceAndCalculateTax → recalculate cart
292:   │     └── Continue to step 4
293:   │
294:   ├── 4. Replace offers in DB:
295:   │     ├── Feature flag: allowFreeGiftWithOffers?
296:   │     │     ├── YES → replaceOffersPreservingFreeGifts
297:   │     │     │     └── Delete all non-FREE_GIFT offers → insert new offers
298:   │     │     └── NO  → replaceExistingOffers
299:   │     │           └── Delete ALL offers → insert new offers
300:   │     │
301:   │     │   DB writes:
302:   │     │     DELETE FROM offer WHERE cartId = ?
303:   │     │     INSERT INTO offer (...) VALUES (...) -- for each offer
304:   │
305:   ├── 5. Update cart prices in DB:
306:   │     ├── Cart.Queries.updateCartWithDiscount(cartId, totalDiscount, totalPrice)
307:   │     │   UPDATE cart SET total_discount=?, total_price=?, updated_at=now()
308:   │     │                WHERE id=? AND is_active=True
309:   │     └── If updateShippingOnOfferUpdate flag: recalculate shipping too
310:   │
311:   └── 6. Return: PUTOfferResponse { cart, offers, hyperPayPayload }
312: ```
313: 
314: #### Remove Flow
315: 
316: Same entry point, but `offerAction = REMOVE`:
317: 
318: ```
319: Product/Offer.putOffer → handlePUTOfferRequest
320:   ├── Platform/Offer.removeOffer (dispatch by ShopType)
321:   │     └── Call platform API to remove discount code
322:   ├── replaceExistingOffers (replace with platform's updated offer list)
323:   ├── Offer.Utils.updatePriceAndCalculateTax → recalculate cart
324:   └── Return: PUTOfferResponse
325: ```
326: 
327: #### Remove Free Gift (special case)
328: 
329: ```
330: Product/Offer.putOffer → handleRemoveCartItemRequest
331:   ├── Delete matching offer records (issuer IN (FREE_GIFT, SHOP))
332:   ├── Delete matching CartItem records
333:   ├── Remove line item from Shopify checkout (if Shopify)
334:   ├── Recalculate cart totals from remaining items
335:   └── Return: PUTOfferResponse
336: ```
337: 
338: #### Price Recalculation (updatePriceAndCalculateTax)
339: 
340: When an offer is applied/removed, cart prices are recalculated:
341: 
342: ```haskell
343: -- For Breeze offers (simple):
344: newTotalDiscount = totalDiscount + offerDiscount
345: newTotalPrice    = totalPrice - offerDiscount
346: 
347: -- For platform offers with tax (complex):
348: taxableAmount        = totalPrice - tax - shippingCharge - surcharge
349: updatedTaxableAmount = taxableAmount - offerDiscount
350: 
351: IF ShopType == SHOPIFY AND issuer == CUSTOM_OFFERS:
352:   updatedTax = originalTax              -- preserve platform's tax
353: ELSE:
354:   baseTax        = originalTax - shippingTax
355:   taxRatio       = baseTax / taxableAmount
356:   updatedBaseTax = updatedTaxableAmount × taxRatio
357:   updatedTax     = updatedBaseTax + shippingTax
358: 
359: newTotalPrice = totalPrice - offerDiscount - originalTax + updatedTax
360: ```
361: 
362: #### Offer Replacement on Cart Update
363: 
364: When cart items change (e.g., quantity update), platform offers may need to be re-synced:
365: 
366: ```
367: Offer.Main.replaceExistingOffers(cartId, newOffers)
368:   ├── Delete all existing offers for cartId
369:   ├── Create new offer records from platform response
370:   └── Recalculate cart prices
371: 
372: Offer.Main.replaceOffersPreservingFreeGifts(cartId, newOffers)
373:   ├── Delete all non-FREE_GIFT offers for cartId
374:   ├── Create new offer records from platform response
375:   └── Return: all offers (new platform offers + preserved free gifts)
376: ```
377: 
378: #### DB Write Sequence (complete PUT offer)
379: 
380: ```
381: 1. DELETE FROM offer WHERE cart_id = ?                          -- clear old offers
382: 2. INSERT INTO offer (id, code, title, issuer, ...) VALUES ... -- for each new offer
383: 3. UPDATE cart SET total_discount=?, total_price=?, tax=?, updated_at=now()
384:    WHERE id=? AND is_active=True                                -- update cart totals
385: ```
386: 
387: Optional (depending on flags):
388: - `DELETE FROM cart_item WHERE id = ?` — if free gift removal
389: - `UPDATE cart SET shipping_charge=?, ...` — if shipping recalculation triggered
390:

393: ### Flow 2: Euler/JusPay Offers (List Only — Frontend Applies)
394: 
395: Euler offers are payment-method-specific cashback/discounts from the JusPay payment gateway (e.g., "10% cashback on HDFC credit card", "₹200 off on UPI"). These work fundamentally differently from platform offers:
396: 
397: 1. **Breeze only lists them** — the backend fetches available offers from Euler and returns them to the frontend
398: 2. **Frontend applies them** — the frontend includes the selected offer code when initiating payment via the Euler/HyperPay SDK
399: 3. **No backend call on apply/remove** — the frontend has all the information (amounts, payment method rules) from the list response
400: 4. **Breeze stores the offer ONLY after payment succeeds** — when Euler confirms the payment, the response includes which offers were availed, and Breeze records them
401: 
402: **The backend's role is: list → cache payment method mappings → store after payment.**
403: 
404: #### Step 1: Frontend Requests Available Offers
405: 
406: ```
407: POST /offer/list  (operationId: list-offers)
408:   → Core.hs → listOffers
409:     → Product/Offer.callListOfferV1
410: ```
411: 
412: Request body (`ListOfferRequestV1`):
413: ```json
414: {
415:   "order": { "amount": 150000, "currency": "INR" },
416:   "merchantId": "merchant_123",
417:   "eulerEnv": "PRODUCTION",
418:   "shopUrl": "myshop.breeze.in",
419:   "cartId": "cart_abc123",
420:   "customerEmail": "user@example.com",
421:   "customer": { "name": "...", "phone": "..." }
422: }
423: ```
424: 
425: #### Step 2: Breeze Fetches Offers from Euler
426: 
427: ```
428: Product/Offer.callListOfferV1
429:   ├── Get merchant's Euler API key
430:   ├── Euler/Offer.getOffersListV1
431:   │     └── POST https://api.juspay.in/v1/offers/list
432:   │           Headers: Authorization: Basic <base64(eulerAPIKey:)>
433:   │           Query: ?emi=true
434:   │           Body: ListOfferRequestV1
435:   │
436:   ├── Euler returns raw JSON with offers[]:
437:   │     Each offer contains:
438:   │       offer_code: "HDFC_10PCT"
439:   │       offer_id: "euler_offer_123"
440:   │       offer_rules:
441:   │         payment_instrument:
442:   │           - payment_method_type: "CREDIT_CARD"
443:   │             payment_method: ["VISA", "MASTERCARD"]
444:   │             issuer: ["HDFC"]
445:   │       benefits:
446:   │         - type: "CASHBACK"
447:   │           value: { percentage: 10, max_amount: 20000 }
448:   │       order_breakup:
449:   │         effective_amount: 135000  ← amount after discount
450:   │
451:   ├── Merge with platform-specific offers (if any):
452:   │     Platform/Offer.combineAndValidateEligibleOffers
453:   │     └── Shopify → checkShopifyOffersEligibility (filter by customer type)
454:   │     └── WooCommerce → getWooCommerceOffers
455:   │
456:   └── Return: RequiredListOfferResponse { offers: [ListOffer] }
457: ```
458: 
459: #### Step 3: Offer-Based Locking (Payment Method Caching)
460: 
461: When listing offers, Breeze extracts payment method constraints and caches them in Redis so the frontend knows which offers are valid for which payment methods:
462: 
463: ```
464: Euler/Offer.Main.getOffersListV1
465:   ├── For each offer: extractOfferIdAndPaymentMethods
466:   │     └── Parse offer_rules.payment_instrument[] →
467:   │         [(paymentMethod, paymentMethodType)] pairs
468:   │         e.g., [("VISA", "CREDIT_CARD"), ("MASTERCARD", "CREDIT_CARD")]
469:   │
470:   ├── Cache in Redis: key = "cart_offer_pms:<cartId>"
471:   │     Value = Map { "HDFC_10PCT": [{"method":"VISA","type":"CREDIT_CARD"}, ...] }
472:   │     TTL = offerBasedLockingttl from shop config (default 4 hours)
473:   │
474:   └── Frontend reads this cache to show/hide offers based on selected payment method
475: ```
476: 
477: **The "offer-based locking" feature** (enabled via shop config `offerBasedLockingEnabled`) restricts which payment methods are available when an Euler offer is selected, ensuring the customer can only pay with methods that qualify for the offer.
478: 
479: #### Step 4: Frontend Applies Offer via Euler SDK
480: 
481: **No call comes to Breeze backend.** The frontend:
482: 1. Displays the offers from the list response
483: 2. When user selects an offer, validates that the selected payment method matches the offer's `payment_instrument` rules
484: 3. Passes the `offer_code` to the Euler/HyperPay SDK when initiating payment
485: 4. Euler SDK handles the offer application during payment processing
486: 
487: The frontend has everything it needs from the list response: offer amounts, payment method rules, order breakup with effective amount.
488: 
489: #### Step 5: After Payment Succeeds — Offer Stored in Breeze DB
490: 
491: When payment completes at Euler, the order status response includes which offers were availed:
492: 
493: ```
494: Euler order response includes:
495:   offers: [
496:     {
497:       offer_id: "euler_offer_123",
498:       offer_code: "HDFC_10PCT",
499:       status: "AVAILED",
500:       benefits: [
501:         { amount: 15000 }   ← discount in paisa
502:       ]
503:     }
504:   ]
505: ```
506: 
507: Breeze processes this during order status resolution:
508: 
509: ```
510: Services/Internal/Offer/Main.validateAndInsertBreezeOffers
511:   ├── Filter: only offers with status == AVAILED
512:   ├── For each availed Euler offer:
513:   │     getBreezeOfferFromEulerOffer(cartId, eulerOffer)
514:   │       → Offer {
515:   │           id: "<cartId>_<eulerOfferId>"
516:   │           code: "<offer_code>"
517:   │           title: "<offer_code>"
518:   │           issuer: BREEZE          ← stored as BREEZE, not EULER
519:   │           issuerOfferId: Just "<eulerOfferId>"
520:   │           cartId: "<cartId>"
521:   │           discount: sum(benefit.amount)   ← total discount in paisa
522:   │           discountedAmount: Just <transactionAmount>
523:   │           autoApply: True
524:   │         }
525:   │
526:   ├── Delete any existing BREEZE offers for this cart
527:   │     DELETE FROM offer WHERE cartId = ? AND issuer = 'BREEZE'
528:   │
529:   ├── Insert new Euler offer records
530:   │     INSERT INTO offer (...) VALUES (...)
531:   │
532:   └── Update cart with offer amounts
533:         updateCartWithEulerOffers(cartId, offers)
534:         → Recalculate totalDiscount and totalPrice
535: ```
536: 
537: **Key: Euler offers are stored with `issuer = BREEZE`** (not a separate EULER issuer). They're distinguished by having a non-null `issuerOfferId` which contains the Euler offer ID.
538: 
539: #### Timeline Comparison
540: 
541: ```
542: PLATFORM OFFER:
543:   Customer enters code → PUT /offer → backend applies → DB updated → response
544:   [────── immediate ──────]
545: 
546: EULER OFFER:
547:   List offers → frontend shows → user selects → SDK payment → payment succeeds → DB updated
548:   [─── list ──]                                [── no backend calls ──]  [── webhook/poll ──]
549: ```

553: ### Flow 3: Breeze Offer Engine (OfferCode)
554: 
555: Merchants can configure custom offer codes via the Breeze dashboard with JS-based eligibility and discount rules. These are stored in the `OfferCode` table and evaluated server-side.

557: ```

563:   ├── OfferCode.calculateDiscount(ruleType, cart)
564:   │     └── Evaluate JS discount rule → returns discount amount
565:   ├── Offer.Main.applyOffer → create Offer record (issuer = BREEZE)
566:   ├── Offer.Utils.updatePriceAndCalculateTax → recalculate cart
567:   └── Return: UpdateOfferResponse
568: ```

599: ### Price Fields
600: 
601: ```
602: initialPrice     = sum(cartItem.price × cartItem.quantity) for all items
603: totalDiscount    = sum(offer.discount) for all active offers
604: shippingCharge   = calculated from shipping rules
605: shippingTax      = tax on shipping
606: shippingDiscount = discount on shipping (if applicable)
607: tax              = product tax
608: surcharge        = payment surcharge (if applicable)
609: 
610: totalPrice = initialPrice - totalDiscount + shippingCharge + shippingTax
611:              - shippingDiscount + tax + surcharge
612: ```
613: 
614: ### Shipping Calculation Modes
615: 
616: `Services/Internal/Cart/Utils.hs` implements 10+ product-based shipping combination modes:
617: 
618: | Mode | Logic |
619: |---|---|
620: | `SUM` | Sum of all item shipping charges |
621: | `SUMWITHQUANTITY` | Sum of (item shipping × quantity) |
622: | `MAX` | Highest single item shipping charge |
623: | `CART_AGGREGATION` | Single shipping rule applied to full cart |
624: | `PERCENTAGE` | Percentage of cart value |
625: | `DEPRIORTIZE_SUMWITHQUANTITY` | SUMWITHQUANTITY but deprioritize certain groups |
626: | `PRIORITIZE_MAX` | MAX but prioritize certain groups |
627: | (and more variants) | Collection-based variants of the above |

631: ## OfferProvider System (Newer Architecture)
632: 
633: The `Services/Internal/OfferProvider/` module implements a clean provider abstraction for the **list offers** operation. This is the correct architecture — new offer listing sources should use this.
634: 
635: ### Typeclass
636: 
637: ```haskell
638: class OfferProvider m provider where
639:   providerType   :: provider -> OfferProviderType
640:   listOffers     :: provider -> ListOffersParams -> m [UnifiedOffer]
641:   getOfferByCode :: provider -> OfferCode -> m (Maybe UnifiedOffer)
642:   getOfferById   :: provider -> OfferId -> m (Maybe UnifiedOffer)
643:   extractMetadata :: provider -> UnifiedOffer -> Maybe OfferMetadata
644: ```

646: ### Provider Registry
647: 
648: ```haskell
649: getProviderForShop :: Shop -> Maybe (ProviderBox Flow)
650: getProviderForShop shop = case shop ^. shopType of
651:   ShopType_SHOPIFY     -> Just $ ProviderBox mkShopifyProvider
652:   ShopType_WOOCOMMERCE -> Nothing  -- Phase 2
653:   _                    -> Nothing
654: ```

657: 
658: ```
659: Service.listOffersForShop:
660:   1. Get platform provider from Registry
661:   2. Fetch from all sources (parallel)
662:   3. Deduplicate by code (platform wins over Euler over native)
663:   4. Sort by ID for stable pagination
664:   5. Apply pagination (offset + limit)
665:   6. Return aggregated list
666: ```

1: # 18 — Configuration System
2: 
3: Vayu uses a **three-tier configuration system**: environment variables (global, immutable at startup), a Redis-stored global config (dynamic, applies to all shops), and per-shop config stored as a JSON column in the `shop` DB table (dynamic, per-merchant). Every shop retrieval automatically merges all three tiers, with shop-level values taking precedence.
4: 
5: ## Architecture Overview
6: 
7: ```
8: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
9: │                    Tier 1: Environment Config                       │
10: │  Loaded once at startup from OS env vars → Config record (immutable)│
11: │  Accessed via: FlowMonad.getConfig <&> (^. Accessor.fieldName)      │
12: │  File: src/Vayu/Config/Config.hs (1609 lines, ~388 fields)         │
13: └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
14:                                │ fallback for
15: ┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
16: │                    Tier 2: Global Config (Redis)                     │
17: │  Stored in Redis key "GLOBAL_CONFIG" as JSON                        │
18: │  Updated via API: POST /global-config (S2S auth, WRITE GLOBAL_CONFIG)│
19: │  Type: GlobalConfig (identical to ShopConfig — allOf: ShopConfig)   │
20: │  File: doc/schemas/global.yaml                                      │
21: └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
22:                                │ fallback for
23: ┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
24: │                    Tier 3: Shop Config (DB)                          │
25: │  Stored in shop.config JSON column per shop                         │
26: │  Updated via API: PATCH /shop/:id/config                            │
27: │  Type: ShopConfig (200+ optional fields)                            │
28: │  File: doc/schemas/shop.yaml (ShopConfig section)                   │
29: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
30: ```
31: 
32: ### Lookup Priority (highest to lowest)
33: 
34: ```
35: Shop Config (DB)  →  Global Config (Redis)  →  Env Config (startup)
36:    non-null?              non-null?              always present
37:    ✓ use it               ✓ use it               ✓ use it (final fallback)
38: ```
39:

47: config' = do
48:   envMap <- EulerLanguage.runIO $ Map.fromList <$> SystemEnvironment.getEnvironment
49:   mkConfigFromEnv envMap

1: # 19 — Authentication System
2: 
3: Vayu uses two parallel authentication systems: **customer tokens** (JWT for end-user sessions) and **S2S tokens** (JWT-based API keys for server-to-server integrations). Every route handler in `Core.hs` explicitly validates one or both before executing business logic.
4: 
5: ## Architecture Overview
6: 
7: ```
8:                           ┌──────────────────────────────┐
9:                           │     HTTP Request              │
10:                           │  Authorization: Bearer <jwt>  │
11:                           │  X-Session-Id: <uuid>         │
12:                           │  X-Shop-URL: <shop_url>       │
13:                           └──────────────┬───────────────┘
14:                                          │
15:                           ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
16:                           │  Middlewares/Request.hs        │
17:                           │  • Add raw-qs, raw-headers    │
18:                           │  • Security headers (Response) │
19:                           └──────────────┬───────────────┘
20:                                          │
21:                           ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
22:                           │  Routes/Core.hs               │
23:                           │  Route handler decides:       │
24:                           │  • S2S only?                  │
25:                           │  • User only?                 │
26:                           │  • Dual (User OR S2S)?        │
27:                           │  • No auth (public)?          │
28:                           └──────────────┬───────────────┘
29:                                          │
30:                ┌─────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
31:                │                                                   │
32:     ┌──────────▼──────────┐                           ┌───────────▼───────────┐
33:     │  Customer Auth       │                           │  S2S Auth              │
34:     │  getBearerTokenData  │                           │  validateS2SAuth       │
35:     │  → JWT verify        │                           │  → Basic or Bearer     │
36:     │  → Check expiry      │                           │  → DB key lookup       │
37:     │  → Extract claims    │                           │  → Access + Route check│
38:     │  → TokenManager      │                           │  → Bool                │
39:     └─────────────────────┘                           └────────────────────────┘
40: ```
41: 
42: ## Header Definitions
43: 
44: All headers are defined in `doc/schemas/commons.yaml` and appear as `Maybe Text` in route handler signatures:
45: 
46: | Header | Purpose | Used By |
47: |--------|---------|---------|
48: | `Authorization` | `Bearer <jwt>` — customer token or S2S token | Both auth flows |
49: | `X-S2s-Token` | Alternate S2S token header (legacy) | Some S2S endpoints |
50: | `X-Super-User` | Basic auth for superuser operations | Key generation |
51: | `X-Session-Id` | Session UUID for request tracing | All endpoints |
52: | `X-Shop-URL` | Shop domain for request context | All endpoints |
53: | `x-request-id` | Request UUID for tracing/logging | All endpoints |
54: | `X-Testing-Mode` | `"true"` to enable testing mode | All endpoints |
55: | `X-Device-Id` | Device UUID for tracking | All endpoints |
56: 
57: **Route parameter order** (must match Servant type): path captures → query params → request body → headers (in declaration order). All headers are `Maybe Text` even if marked required in YAML.

1: # 20 — Notification Engine
2: 
3: Vayu has a multi-channel, multi-provider notification system supporting **SMS**, **WhatsApp**, **Email**, and **Push Notifications (FCM)**. 10: │  Product/MessageService.hs — exposes all notification APIs            │
11: │  Product/OtpService.hs — OTP-specific dispatch                        │
12: │  Product/Identity/Login/OTP/Dispatch.hs — type class channel dispatch │
13: └──────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────┘
14:            │                                         │
15:            ▼                                         ▼
16: ┌─────────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────────┐
17: │  Services/Internal       │            │  Credential & Template       │
18: │  MessageService.hs       │            │  Queries/MessageCredentials  │
19: │  • sendSMS               │            │  Queries/MessageTemplate     │
